answer: Each agent may serve only one exclusive data-availability slice. A juniper allocator maps live keys onto non-overlapping chunks. At every dawn proof window, the agent must publish an availability proof; accepted proofs are compacted into a public shale log of chunk commitments. If two keys prove the same slice, both locked bonds are slashed and the slice is reissued. To operate N identities, an attacker provisions N independent storage capacities, locks N bonds, and maintains N distinct proofs at each dawn, so hardware, capital, and operating cost all scale with farm size.
